runtime.command_template: python -B tools/run_pinmame_harness.py --library <pinned-pinmame64.dll> --game nbaf_31 --rom-path <vpinmame-roms> --work-dir <new-isolated-state> --handle-mechanics 1 --scenario tools/harness-scenarios/wpc-95/nbaf-motor-test.json --dmd-dir <external-dmd-dir> --output <external-run.json>. PinMAME's built-in defender mechanism (mech slot 0, handle-mechanics 1) answers the motor outputs with the position switches 51-55, so the run shows the ROM's own contract with that model: which outputs it drives for each named move and which position the model then reports. It is a synthetic probe, not a measurement of the physical defender.

named_action_observations.label: T.16 self-test runs the defender to POS 4 with the motor (37) and direction (38) outputs, mirrored at 41 and 42
T.16 MOVE LEFT drives the motor enable 37 alone (mirror 41) and the marked position moves from POS 4 to POS 3
T.16 MOVE RIGHT drives 37 with the direction line 38 (mirrors 41, 42) and the marked position moves from POS 3 back to POS 4
During T.16 the ROM pulses the shot clock enable (39) and count (40) lines; PinMAME's nbaf.c turns them into the two-digit display 1, which counts down (23, 22, ... 11, ...)

raw_runs.name: nbaf_31-motor-test
raw_runs.nvram_initialization: empty; the run created its own isolated PinMAME state directory, so the ROM performed its own factory reset before the scenario left the message loop with Escape

source.attribution: Generated locally from pinned PinMAME and the user-authorized ROM corpus; ROM bytes remain external. Public switch writes are host stimuli, never ROM observations. The runner can checkpoint only segment-display text, so the DMD service-menu navigation is counted pulses; every diagnostic snapshot's interpreted_text is the curator's visual reading of its retained DMD frame, identified by its pixel SHA-256. The exact external directory manifest (built by tools/build_external_evidence_manifest.py) lists the raw trace, the copied scenario, the DMD frames and the isolated mutable state, with no ROM bytes.
